thread:
rachel: Heads-up: Partner-Ops reported a partial-apply incident where their "ready" manifest uploaded to S3, but our ingestion crashed mid-apply and only half the hourly rows landed. Result: customers saw partial entitlements and out-of-balance ledger.

diego: ouch. do we have reproducible steps?

partner-ops: summary: upload manifest mf-2026-03-21 with per-hour files to s3://partner-mft/day=2026-03-21/, then send webhook to /partner/notify. Our webhook was retried twice and our worker started applying each hourly file without an atomic commit across the manifest. Worker crashed after applying first 3/12 hours.

priya: long story short: we need an atomic commit protocol for partner manifests. propose lightweight two-phase commit: 1) partner uploads per-hour files + manifest with checksum and manifest_uuid; 2) partner POSTs /partner/prepare with manifest_uuid, we reserve a ledger_tx_id and validate checksums; 3) Redwood responds READY; 4) partner POSTs /partner/commit manifest_uuid + signed token; 5) ingestion runs apply_all within a single DB transaction or an idempotent multi-row upsert that tags ledger_tx_id as committed. If commit fails, we mark manifest as aborted and run compensating reverse for partial rows.

infra-bot: created PARTNER-3780: "Atomic manifest commit + manifest lifecycle" assigned to diego. https://redwood.internal/partners/3780

rachel: important constraints: 1) manifests can be large, so avoid locking the entire billing table for hours. We should use a commit record pattern: write per-hour provisional rows with column committed=false and ledger_tx_id; after all rows present and validated, flip committed=true in a single atomic update for that tx id. Billing pipeline only sums committed rows.

diego: implementation sketch: per-hour insert as upsert (partner_id, hour, provisional_units, ledger_tx_id) then at end: UPDATE partner_hourly_agg SET committed = true WHERE ledger_tx_id = 'tx-UUID'; this avoids long transactions while preventing partial count in billing.

priya: add checksum guard: manifest file has manifest_checksum = sha256(concat(file1_checksum...)). On prepare we validate each file checksum against S3 etag and reject if mismatch. Also require TTL on prepare tokens (e.g., 1h) so old prepared manifests can be garbage-collected.

billing: note: billing runners must be updated to only consider committed=true and handle late-commit windows. Also add an alert when a manifest is prepared but not committed after 30m.

partner-ops: we can modify our uploader to perform prepare+commit handshake. We'll generate manifest_uuid and sign commit token with our key. ETA: 48h after API spec.

rachel: compensating flow: if partial commits were applied previously, we need an automated correction job that looks for ledger_tx_id where some hours missing or manifest marked aborted and then computes reverse deltas. SQL prototype to detect partials: ```sql
SELECT ledger_tx_id, count(*) AS applied_count, sum(case when committed then 1 else 0 end) AS committed_count
FROM partner_hourly_agg
WHERE manifest_uuid = 'mf-2026-03-21'
GROUP BY ledger_tx_id
HAVING committed_count = 0 OR applied_count < expected_file_count;
```
Then generate correction rows of type='reversal' referencing original ledger_tx_id.

priya: tests: 1) simulate crash mid-apply and ensure no committed rows until commit call; 2) simulate duplicate commit attempts and ensure idempotence; 3) simulate prepare token expiry and ensure manifest is rejected. Add integration tests under integration/partners/partner-atomic/commit.spec.ts.

diego: dev estimate: API + prepare/commit handshake + provisional path ~2d, billing runner filter + alerts ~1d, tests + docs ~1d. We'll target rollout by next Thu.

rachel: comms: partner onboarding doc + partner playbook must be updated to require prepare/commit; include example cURL flow and error codes. @priya will write partner-facing spec.

partner-ops: we'll pause large replays until handshake is live. We'll also provide signed manifests for the problematic day to help reconciliation.

billing: when rolling out, ensure a soft-launch window where manifests are still treated as pre-apply unless partner uses the new handshake. We'll also surface a reconciliation report summarizing manifests applied vs reversed over 7 days.

priya: I'll open PR for API spec and draft the doc. rachel, diego, want to review before we send to partners.

rachel: thanks all. daily standup to followup tomorrow 9:00 PT. :white_check_mark:
